title: Verify and commit payment protocol data round-trip refactor
description: Run vitest for payment-protocol-data.spec.ts, npx nx affected:build and affected:lint, then commit the five changed files on feat/agentic-payment-tokens.

title: Fix protocol data value typing to match PaymentProtocolDataSchema (value: string)
description: parseProtocolDataField in packages/commercetools/src/core/payment-protocol-data.ts returns value: unknown, but PaymentProtocolDataSchema requires value: z.string() and checkout.factory.ts asserts satisfies PaymentInstruction. Keep string values as-is, JSON.stringify non-string JSON values; type serializeProtocolData input as {key, value: string}[].

title: Core: consent management (capability or personalizationProfile extension)
description:
UCP's buyer consent extension (extensions/buyer-consent.md) lets platforms submit buyer consent per purpose (dev.ucp.consent.analytics / marketing / preferences / sale_or_sharing, plus channel segments like marketing.email/sms), each with granted and source (business default vs platform-captured buyer choice). Today the UCP layer only round-trips it on the checkout session (not persisted, extension not advertised).

Decide between a dedicated consent-management capability or extending PersonalizationProfileCapability (currently read-only: getPersonalizationProfile with segments/blurb) with typed get/record-consent mutations and schemas. Implement in the CDP-backed providers (unomi; fake; commercetools/medusa/hcl as applicable).

Record provenance with each decision for GDPR accountability (when, how, for what): e.g. captured via UCP, the platform's agent profile, the checkout session, timestamp - as typed fields, not a free-form bag. Then: persist consent on checkout create/update/complete, advertise dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent with the business defaults (source: business) in responses.

title: commercetools: cart/checkout factory price breakdown (totalProductPrice, line discounts)
description: Found while mapping UCP discounts: (1) CommercetoolsCartFactory sets totalProductPrice = totalPrice - shipping, i.e. the product total AFTER discounts (and including tax for net-priced projects), while UCP needs the undiscounted subtotal - the UCP layer now derives it from line items as a workaround. Decide and document the core semantics of CostBreakDown.totalProductPrice (before or after discounts?) and align all providers. (2) parseCartItem adds lineItem.price.discounted.value.centAmount (the discounted PRICE) to totalDiscount, which overstates line discounts when product discounts apply; it should add price.value - price.discounted.value per unit. Check the checkout and order factories for the same.

title: commercetools: include automatic cart discounts in Cart.appliedPromotions
description: Cart.appliedPromotions is meant to list every promotion applied to the cart, with isCouponCode=false for automatic ones and true for user-entered codes. The commercetools cart factory (packages/commercetools/src/factories/cart/cart.factory.ts) only maps cart.discountCodes, so automatic cart discounts (applied when items are added) are missing. Map the cart discounts referenced by lineItems[].discountedPricePerQuantity[].discountedPrice.includedDiscounts and discountOnTotalPrice.includedDiscounts (expand the cart discount references for name/description), de-duplicated, as isCouponCode=false entries - and distinguish code-triggered cart discounts (requiresDiscountCode) so they are not listed twice. Check the checkout factory too.

title: Core: Promotion.amount as the actual monetary amount discounted by each promotion
description: PromotionSchema (packages/core/src/schemas/models/price.model.ts) has an optional amount, described as 'if applicable/available from the source system'; the commercetools factory never sets it. Make it the actual monetary amount discounted by that promotion/adjustment on this cart (summed over line items and the cart total), populated by every provider (commercetools, medusa, magento, hcl, fake), and consider making it required. Consumer: the UCP discount extension's discounts.applied[].amount and allocations, which today fall back to aggregate line/cart discounts. Core schema change - needs clearance; implement in all providers.

title: Core: typed order-callback info on cart/checkout capability (discuss first)
description:
Add provider-neutral metadata to carts and cart items, following the PaymentInstruction.protocolData pattern ({key, value} strings, round-tripped by providers).

Core: Cart.metadata and CartItem.metadata; optional metadata on cart.add, plus cart.setMetadata / cart.setItemMetadata mutations. Checkout and Order expose what they inherit from the cart.

commercetools: a JSON custom field on the cart type (like reactionaryProtocolData on payments) and a line-item custom type; commercetools orders inherit cart and line-item custom fields, so the data reaches the order and the OMS natively. Other providers: map onto their equivalent (e.g. Medusa metadata).

First consumer: UCP order webhooks. Order updates (shipped, delivered, refunds) are known to the backend/OMS, not reactionary, which only captures the order. On completion, UCP would write ucp_order_webhook_url (from the platform's agent profile, order capability config.webhook_url - one URL per platform), ucp_agent_profile and ucp_checkout_session_id, so the OMS can post signed order-updated events itself (it needs the business signing key; see signatures.md). Reactionary keeps sending only the 'Order created' event.

Changes the core schemas - additive, but check clearance for provider implementations.
notes: MUST BE DISCUSSED BEFORE EXECUTION. Design constraint: reactionary avoids any-typed / free-form calls, so an untyped key/value metadata bag is likely not acceptable as proposed. Preferred direction: dedicated, strongly typed capability methods, each with its own mutation and mutation schema, to record order-event callback information (webhook URL, platform profile, originating checkout session) - on the core cart capability, or on the checkout capability if it only matters at checkout. Must then be implemented in every provider (commercetools, medusa, magento, hcl, fake, ...). Revisit whether per-item metadata is still needed under that design.

title: UCP: decide policy for raw card (PAN) credentials on non-test handlers
description: completeCheckoutSession forwards any instrument credential verbatim into the payment's ucp_payment_credential protocol data, which commercetools persists in the reactionaryProtocolData custom field until the payment extension replaces it. A raw card credential (type 'card', card_number_type fpan, number/cvc) would therefore be stored in commercetools - a PCI scope concern. Decide whether to reject raw card credentials unless a handler explicitly opts in, or document it. Behaviour change for consumers - needs clearance before changing.
close_reason: Raw card credentials (pan/card, or carrying number/cvc) are refused with payment_failed and never forwarded, unless acceptRawCardCredentials is set; the harness advertises token-only request_constraints on the Stripe handler. Spec: credentials are opaque tokens, not raw PANs; pan_credential is source-only.

title: MCP: verify a checkout can be completed end-to-end via the MCP endpoints
description: Verify that an agent can take a checkout from cart to placed order using only the MCP server's tools (packages/mcp), against a real backend (commercetools test project), including payment with a delegated credential. Cover the happy path and a declined payment; add an e2e test if feasible. File follow-ups for any gaps found.

title: UCP: support AP2 mandate, token-binding, and raw card credential completion
description: ap2_test, binding_test and card_credential_test complete with credential types the Stripe extension cannot confirm synchronously (not pm_/spt_), so completion polls the authorization wait and the suite's HTTP client times out. Needs a decision per credential type: confirm (e.g. raw card via Stripe test tokens), reject spec-shaped as payment_failed, or support AP2 mandates. Also investigate validation_test.py::test_complete_without_fulfillment and test_update_inventory_validation ReadTimeouts (same completion path).
close_reason: Unadvertised handlers rejected fast (payment_failed); testPaymentHandlers option + conformance mock handler mapped to Stripe test PMs; billing address no longer stands in for a shipping destination. ap2/binding/card_credential/complete_without_fulfillment pass live; update_inventory now fails only on mqp's error code.

title: UCP: emit order-event webhooks (order created/updated, signed deliveries)
description: The suite registers a webhook sink and expects fully-populated order entities on order creation/update, with standard webhook headers, signatures covering the UCP-Agent, and retry semantics. No webhooks are sent today. Fails all 6 webhook_structure_test.py tests and webhook_test.py::test_webhook_event_stream.
notes: testOrderUpdates (PUT /orders/{id}, test-only) now exists on the stack (PR for a1w); order updates posted through it are the natural trigger for order-updated webhooks. UCP order records (store.getOrder) carry checkoutSessionId/agentProfile.
close_reason: Opt-in webhooks option: Order created/updated events as full order entities to the platform profile's webhook_url, Standard Webhooks headers, RFC 9421 signatures (ES256/ES384/Ed25519), retries preserving event identity. Long-term, updates should come from the OMS - see reactionary-dv2.

title: UCP: order endpoint returns actual order data
description: handleGetOrder in packages/ucp/src/lib/reactionary-ucp-rest.ts stubs required fields: empty line_items, empty checkout_id, empty fulfillment.expectations/events. Fails conformance order_test.py::test_order_fulfillment_retrieval ('No options returned') and test_order_update. Map the reactionary order's items, originating checkout id, and fulfillment data into the UCP order schema.
close_reason: GET /orders maps real order data (line items, checkout_id, fulfillment expectations from the selected option); order access restricted to the placing session + platform or a linked identity (backend /me/orders scoping); PUT /orders behind test-only testOrderUpdates. order_test.py + invalid_input_test.py pass live.

title: UCP: buyer consent in the checkout view
description: Responses lack applied-discounts and buyer-consent fields. Fails conformance business_logic_test.py::test_discount_flow, test_multiple_discounts_one_rejected, test_buyer_consent. Needs discount codes surfaced in the checkout view. Test data is ready: the commercetools test project has TESTCODE1 (absolute discount, 15.00 DKK — ProportionateDistribution; also 2 EUR/3 USD) wired into examples/node/conformance/test_fixtures.json as valid_fixed_discount_code, and BOGO (relative 100% on a target). The suite's conformance currency is DKK.
notes:
Latest conformance suite adds business_logic_test.py::test_fixed_amount_discount (expects 1500 discount, gets 0) - same gap: applied discounts not surfaced.
Discount part done (phase 1, PR on feat/ucp-discounts): discount extension on checkout sessions. Remaining: buyer consent (business_logic_test.py::test_buyer_consent, extensions/buyer-consent.md). Follow-ups: reactionary-bi6, -d9i, coupon rejection reasons, /carts discounts, commercetools price breakdown, suite items_discount deviation.
close_reason: Discounts: phase 1 PR (#221). Buyer consent: round-tripped on the checkout session (both the spec purpose map and the SDK's flat booleans), not persisted and not advertised; real consent storage in reactionary-0sn.

title: UCP: map unpurchasable/out-of-stock line items to item_unavailable/out_of_stock error codes
description: Unpurchasable and out-of-stock items are reported with code 'missing' instead of the spec's standard codes item_unavailable/out_of_stock (error_code.json / checkout.md). Fails conformance validation_test.py::test_out_of_stock, test_structured_error_messages, test_update_inventory_validation. Likely where line-item errors are built in packages/ucp/src/lib/reactionary-ucp-checkout-session.ts / reactionary-ucp-rest.ts.
notes: test_update_inventory_validation no longer times out (reactionary-d88); it now fails only on the error code ('missing' instead of out_of_stock/item_unavailable).
close_reason: Opt-in inventory option (fulfillmentCenterKeys) reports out_of_stock per line item; conformance data uses 7313020077406 (in stock) and 7313020065489 (out of stock). Diagnosis in the bead was off: no line-item error was emitted at all; 'missing' came from other inputs.

description: caching.spec.ts (1) and identity.spec.ts (2) fail with 'No published product with an sku 0766623301831 exists'. Test data issue in the live commercetools project, not code. Republish the product or update the fixture SKU.

description: After PR #224 the UCP conformance suite runs 62 passed / 3 failed / 12 skipped against the commercetools test project. Shared test-data additions (need agreement before changing the shared project) would unlock: (1) an ORDER-level discount code (target totalPrice) -> the 3 discount_test.py failures + totals_test.py:174 skip (see reactionary-lf7); (2) a second, ideally percentage, discount code -> business_logic_test::test_multiple_discounts_accepted and discount_test::test_codes_replace_previous_set (fixtures valid_discount_code_2, expected_discount_percentage[_2]); (3) a product with item-based free shipping -> fulfillment_test::test_free_shipping_for_specific_item (fixture free_shipping_item_sku). title: UCP: discount extension on cart resources (/carts)
description: Phase 1 of the discount extension (PR for reactionary-r2o) advertises dev.ucp.shopping.discount extending dev.ucp.shopping.checkout only. Extend /carts create/update/get the same way (discounts.codes in, discounts.applied out, items_discount/discount totals) via the shared reactionary-ucp-discounts helpers, and advertise extends: [cart, checkout]. Cart-to-checkout continuity already holds: checkout sessions over a cart_id reuse the reactionary cart, whose codes carry into the checkout.

title: UCP conformance: discount_test.py only accepts a 'discount' total, not 'items_discount'
description: discount_test.py (test_code_matches_case_insensitively, test_discount_total_is_negative, test_empty_codes_removes_discount) and totals_test.py:174 look for totals[type=discount] only. discount.md 'Impact on Line Items and Totals' requires line-allocated discounts as items_discount (with line_items[].totals[type=items_discount] summing to it) and only order-level ones as discount; business_logic_test.py accepts both. Our TESTCODE1 is line-level, so we emit items_discount and these 3 tests fail / 1 skips. Raise upstream with Universal-Commerce-Protocol/conformance, or add an order-level test code to the commercetools project for the conformance runs.

title: UCP: payment simulation endpoint with shared-secret header
description: simulation_url_security_test.py expects a simulation endpoint (200 with correct secret, 403 with wrong/missing header); we return 404 as the route does not exist. Part of the spec's testing surface for PSP simulation.
close_reason: testSimulationSecret option enables POST /testing/simulate-shipping/{id} (403 without the right Simulation-Secret), records a shipment and sends the update webhook.

title: UCP: stored-address injection for known customers (only for linked identities)
description: 8 conformance tests skip (fulfillment_test.py known_customer*, webhook_test.py address tests): the suite expects a business to inject a customer's stored addresses as fulfillment destinations when the buyer EMAIL matches a known customer. Deliberately not implemented: doing it by email alone exposes stored addresses to anyone who knows an email. If wanted, do it only for OAuth2-linked buyers (bearer session -> profile capability addresses), which the suite does not exercise.

title: Core: optional human-readable reason when a coupon code is rejected
description: UCP's discount extension reports rejected codes as discount_code_expired / _invalid / _already_applied / _combination_disallowed / _user_not_logged_in / _user_ineligible. cart.applyCouponCode only fails with a generic error, so the UCP layer reports every rejection as discount_code_invalid. Add a typed rejection reason (a dedicated error type/enum in the mutation result, no free-form data) and map it in every provider. commercetools has the information: addDiscountCode errors and cart.discountCodes[].state (NotActive, NotValid, DoesNotMatchCart, MaxApplicationReached, ApplicationStoppedByPreviousDiscount) - note a code can be accepted onto the cart yet not match it, which today still shows as applied. Core schema change - needs clearance; all providers.
notes: Rescoped (per discussion): backends generally cannot say WHY a code was rejected, so the UCP code stays discount_code_invalid - no typed reason enum. Instead: an optional free-form, human-readable reason string on the applyCouponCode rejection (still a typed field, not an any-bag), passed through as the UCP warning content. Providers fill it when they know something (e.g. commercetools discountCodes[].state such as DoesNotMatchCart / MaxApplicationReached; also catches codes accepted onto the cart that do not actually apply). Low priority.

title: UCP: guest orders are not visible after OAuth2 identity linking
description: An order placed as a guest is readable only from the placing session/platform. commercetools login (CommercetoolsAPI.login) does not sign in with the guest's anonymousId, so after the buyer links their account (OAuth2 identity linking) in a later session, /me/orders does not return orders they placed as a guest before linking. Decide whether login should assign anonymous orders to the customer (commercetools sign-in with anonymousId) - affects all reactionary consumers, not just UCP.
notes: Not required: orders placed while OAuth2-linked are readable from later OAuth2 sessions (verified live). This only covers guest orders placed before linking.
